reason: The text fragment is a narrative from Genesis 27 describing the deception of Isaac by Jacob, with assistance from Rebekah, to obtain the patriarchal blessing intended for Esau. The passage involves family conflict and personal betrayal within the patriarchal household, but contains no reference to the Hebrew people as a collective body or to any complaints directed at leaders. While Esau does cry out in distress upon discovering the deception, this is a personal/family grievance, not a communal complaint about leadership. The statement requires evidence of the Hebrew people (as a collective entity) voicing complaints about their leaders, which is entirely absent from this text.
